STAGE 1 — goal: check each of the four proposals against the six scope criteria (esp. criterion 6, baseline Sinkhorn must be kept) and against the frozen evidence, then rank.
READ: the four proposal texts and the four frozen evidence bundles (6f9f3944ba78d62b = successor-anchor; 442c7bd52814c269 = fine-residual geodesic transport; adeb64486765c2fd = poincare residual-direction; 65930410bd2f75d8 = bgcd-fine), rubric rank-2026-10-v1.
OBSERVED:
- All four bundles share the identical sanity block: E11 geometry_operator_valid PASS (log0(exp0(v)) err 2.78e-17, curvature -0.5, curved/euclid ratio 1.4285); E12 behavior_dependency FAIL (positive row scalar cannot move any argmin; codeword-dependent weight moved 0% of top-1; codeword-independent offset also invariant); E13 geometry_dependency PASS (Euclid intervention moved 1 of top-1); E14 joint_path_dependency CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN. So E12/E14 are a GENERIC proxy result applied to all four and do NOT differentiate; the coupling is unverified for every proposal.
- E5 OK: train transition graph 115582 edges, mean out-degree 5.45 (so successor signals are dense enough to be computed).
- E6 OK (diagnostic only): baseline same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067 — baseline SIDs barely encode behaviour, i.e. headroom exists for a behaviour-aware fine layer.
- Prior-work match labels differ: fine-residual is 'related_but_different' to HVQ-VAE/HyperVQ/E8 (E17-E19), the other three are 'same_operator_or_path'. Novelty is not a scope criterion, used only as a tiebreak.
- Criterion 6: successor-anchor explicitly "no argmin anywhere, P2=baseline Sinkhorn(C2)"; poincare-residual "take the plan's argmax column"; fine-residual "code index taken from it exactly as baseline"; bgcd "no argmin replaces the plan". ALL FOUR KEEP THE BALANCED PLAN -> none out of scope on criterion 6.
REASONING (rank): (1) poincare-residual-direction wins on derivation of constants (kappa_l=-1/R_l^2 from measured residual median, eps_l scaled by measured mean(C)/mean(C_euclid)) and on the radius-preserving tangential bias that structurally forbids pulling residuals onto one code — the exact anti-collapse property the measured 955-prefix/0.771-collision round lacked. (2) fine-residual geodesic transport: L1 untouched, bounded Mobius translation under the baseline temperature, isometry=bijection so it structurally cannot merge, and it is the most differentiated from prior work; below #1 only because c=1 is a fixed contract default rather than a measured curvature and its own risk admits pure permutation of codewords. (3) bgcd: repulsive code displacement with derived m_i cap and L1 untouched, but a per-(i,k) code displacement makes the cost non-metric, costs a full extra forward pass per epoch (+5-7%) and adds an ill-conditioning route via the min-over-codes cap. (4) successor-anchor: C2 = d2_r/a_i - beta*d2_b/m_i MINIMISES TWO SQUARED DISTANCES, i.e. it is an ATTRACTOR to the successor anchor — the same cohesion mechanism that ate fine resolution last round; its own hypothesis (prefixes stay >=7414) is in tension with its attractive form, and declaring the equal median-normalised weighting "neutral" is asserted, not derived.
OPEN: nothing measurable; no arm is trained this round. Final ranking recorded next.

STAGE 2 (FINAL ANSWER) — ranking of all four proposals, rubric rank-2026-10-v1, grounded in the frozen bundles.

The binding reservation is shared and unverified across all four: every bundle carries the identical E12 FAIL (the generic positive-row-scalar and codeword-independent-offset manipulations leave the argmin unchanged) and E14 joint_path_dependency CANDIDATE_PATH_NOT_RUN, so none of the four has demonstrated the coupling it claims, and no bundle contains any Stage3 Recall observation.
